answer: Proof of Personhood via biometric verification acts as a violet barrier, forcing Sybil attackers to bridge an ocean of physical authentication costs. By requiring agents to bind unique identity to a sparrow of cryptographic entropy—a single, non-transferable digital signature—the network imposes a linear scaling cost on identity fabrication. An attacker must procure distinct human-verified credentials for every node, effectively making the marginal cost of a fake identity prohibitive relative to any network gain.
